stories.headline: A family turned a mined-out reef island back into a bird haven
stories.summary: Guano mining in the 1860s left Lady Elliot Island bare for a century. From the 1960s the Adams family began replanting; now over 20,000 plants cover about 70% of it and seabirds nest again.
stories.why: Patient, hands-on work brought a whole ecosystem back to life.

stories.headline: A super-sweet fruit protein halved blood sugar spikes
stories.summary: In a double-blind trial, ice cream sweetened with brazzein, a protein first found in a West African fruit, caused blood sugar rises about half as big as sugar ice cream did.
stories.why: Sweet treats that are kinder to blood sugar could help people with diabetes.

stories.headline: A 6,500-year-old clay figurine turns up in Transylvania
stories.summary: At the Dâmbul Cetății site, archaeologists found a Copper Age female figurine of the Cucuteni culture. It cracked exactly where its maker joined two pieces of clay, revealing how it was made.
stories.why: A crack 6,500 years in the making shows us an ancient artist's technique.

stories.stat_label: young humpbacks back in open water
stories.headline: Rescuers helped stranded young humpbacks back to the sea
stories.summary: Two juvenile humpback whales got stuck on sandbars off Fire Island. With rising tides and help from crews including the US Coast Guard, both made it back to open water.
stories.why: Quick teamwork gave two young whales a second chance.

fun_fact: Brazzein keeps its sweetness even when heated to 80 °C.
